transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-24
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Lisa (Northbridge Head of Platform), Dan (SecOps), Janelle (ML), Ravi (Compliance)

Summary: Quick demo of request storage toggles, logging/redaction policies, and a scenario of PII ejection + SOC2 questions. Walkthrough focused on API flags, Console toggles, and Optimize suggestions for cost/latency tradeoffs.

00:00 - Ethan: alright, uh hi everyone thanks for taking the time, this is Ethan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Maya our solutions engineer. Can you hear us ok?
00:07 - Lisa: yes, loud and clear. thanks Ethan.
00:10 - Dan: yep, good here.
00:12 - Maya: great. quick agenda, we'll run through the console toggles for request storage, show the API flags for ephemeral requests, demo redaction flow for logs, and then run a short optimize recommendation—just to surface batching/quantization tradeoffs for your telemetry workload.
00:25 - Ravi: good. main ask from compliance is how quickly we can flip off request storage for specific routes and what audit trails remain.
00:32 - Ethan: perfect. we'll show the per-route retention toggle and the audit-log behavior. note up front: toggles can be at route, model, or team level. by default the hosted session keeps telemetry for 30 days for debugging but you can change to ephemeral or none.
00:48 - Janelle: when you say ephemeral, is that zero retention or short TTL? does ephemeral mean KV cache also expires sooner?
00:55 - Maya: good question. ephemeral on Redwood means request payloads are not persisted to request storage; ephemeral telemetry still writes minimal tracing for latency SLOs to our observability product but it is sampled and not correlated to user content. KV cache on the runtime is unrelated—kv cache is in-memory for the session and not persisted to disk unless you opt into request capture. sometimes people conflate those.
01:16 - Lisa: ok that sounds promising. Dan, our concern is logs leaking PII. can you show the redaction pipeline?
01:22 - Maya: sure. i'm going to share my screen. (screen share) so this is the Console -> Data Controls page. top pane is request storage toggles, you can flip between retain, redact-only, ephemeral, or custom. i'm going to toggle route: /api/assistant/finetuned -> set to redact-only.
01:40 - [Maya shares UI click sounds]
01:45 - Maya: redact-only keeps the request body for X hours but runs redaction rules prior to storing. rules can be regex, entity-based, or a pre-trained PII model. i'm enabling a sample regex set that strips SSN, credit card numbers, and a custom pattern your team provided earlier.
02:05 - Dan: sounds good. how do we vet the regex? false negatives are the issue for us.
02:11 - Maya: you can run a dry-run against your corpus inside the Console; it will show matches and false positives. you saw the sample report earlier in the deck. also we support a secondary layer: a classification model that flags possible PII, then you can choose to redact or route to manual review.
02:29 - Ravi: manual review--will that show in audit logs? we need traceability for compliance.
02:34 - Ethan: yes, audit logs persist actions like toggle flips, manual redaction decisions, who approved, and timestamps. those logs are available via the API or S3 export and can be integrated with SIEM. logs contain metadata only—no raw request content if route is set to ephemeral or redact-only.
02:53 - Janelle: what's the timeline for the SOC2 bits? we run yearly audits and need the crosswalk.
02:58 - Ethan: we have SOC2 Type II—I'll attach the report. also KMS key usage and HSM options for Private deployments are documented in the whitepaper.
03:07 - Lisa: great. can we see an example of request capture being toggled programmatically via API? our platform spins up both long-running and short-lived routes.
03:14 - Maya: yes, here's the snippet. (Maya pastes code) POST /v1/routes/:id/storage { "retention": "ephemeral" } -- in practice you can set per-route or pass header x-redwood-retention: ephemeral on a request-by-request basis.
03:32 - Dan: that header approach is interesting. do you apply rate limits or require auth on that header? i worry about someone toggling retention accidentally.
03:38 - Maya: it's guarded by RBAC; only service keys with the retention:write scope can set retention. and every change emits an audit event. also we recommend a canary policy: only allow header-based epithelial toggles from specific IP ranges or service accounts.
03:54 - Ravi: ok that addresses controls. how does this differ for Dedicated and Private? the team is considering private deployment for regulated data.
04:02 - Ethan: in Dedicated, you still have the same toggles but storage endpoints are in your VPC; we don't have access to the raw blobs. in Private on-prem, the control plane is customer-managed—audit logs can be exported to your logging cluster and KMS is your own key. latency and throughput behave similarly but there is an ops delta.
04:22 - Janelle: ops delta meaning more setup and maintenance?
04:24 - Ethan: exactly. Dedicated reduces ops work vs fully private, but gives you the isolation you need. cost is higher for Private due to infra and support.
04:33 - Lisa: show us an example redaction misfire—like when an entity is misclassified.
04:37 - Maya: sure. i'm going to run a sample conversation. (typing) Request: "Customer's card number is 4111-1111-1111-1111 and SSN is 123-45-6789".
04:50 - Maya: result in redact-only mode after rules: "Customer's card number is [REDACTED] and SSN is [REDACTED]". notice the phone number pattern we had previously didn't match because customer used dots, so dry-run flagged that as a false negative.
05:05 - Dan: ah, so we need iterative rule tuning. can the Console keep a history of rule versions?
05:09 - Maya: yes, there's a version history and you can roll back. we also store detection metrics so you can see trends.
05:16 - Ethan: quick interjection—Optimize can recommend a lower-cost model for high-volume telemetry routes where fidelity isn't critical. for high-risk routes you run a higher-privacy model in Private mode. the platform can route requests by policy.
05:34 - Janelle: can Optimize surface batching suggestions that still meet latency SLOs? our inference is very latency-sensitive for chat.
05:41 - Maya: yes—Optimize collects sequence length distributions and suggests batching windows and model configs. for chat you might enable smaller max-batch but higher concurrency; for asynchronous embedding jobs you can increase batch size.
05:54 - Lisa: any examples of where batching caused PII correlation issues?
05:58 - Maya: typical concern is side-channel in shared runtimes. our model of isolation is that we do request-level isolation for KV caches. batching groups requests on the same worker but we do strict per-request separation of state—no cross-request KV leakage. plus we support per-customer tenancy on Dedicated so that risk is eliminated.
06:17 - Dan: good. about retention toggles: if we flip a route from retain -> ephemeral, do you purge existing stored requests?
06:23 - Maya: there are two flows: you can flip and mark historic data for TTL-based purge, or you can request immediate purge which creates a job that deletes objects and emits an audit event. immediate purge is an irreversible operation and we log it.
06:37 - Ravi: is there a way to escrow request data for legal hold? sometimes legal asks to preserve certain sessions.
06:42 - Ethan: yes, there's a legal-hold feature—it's an opt-in retention policy that overrides ephemeral. it's gated by compliance roles and we store proofs of access in the audit log.
06:55 - Lisa: okay, moving to practicalities—can you run a pilot that includes our PII regex set and sample workload? we'd like to see false negative rate and throughput impact.
07:03 - Maya: absolutely. we can provision a sandbox in Dedicated or hosted pilot; recommended path is hosted pilot with dedicated tenant to keep ops small. we'll run a dry-run redaction and a benchmark for your distribution.
07:16 - Janelle: what's the throughput impact of running redaction pre-store? do you do it inline or asynchronously?
07:21 - Maya: redaction is inline for redact-only so it's deterministic; you will see a slight CPU increase but we can parallelize across workers. in high-throughput routes we recommend an async pipeline for non-blocking ingestion—request is accepted and redaction runs in a sidecar before write, but then you'd need stronger guarantees for sync-sensitive paths.
07:37 - Dan: that tradeoff is exactly what we weigh. have you measured token-level latency impact?
07:41 - Maya: yes, I have a quick chart. for typical chat payloads under 1k tokens redaction adds ~8-20ms median per request depending on rule complexity. CPU-bound regexes can spike higher. for 90th percentile careful tuning reduces spikes.
07:58 - Lisa: can you email that chart and the benchmark spreadsheet?
08:02 - Ethan: will do. i'll attach the spreadsheet and the redaction benchmark. link in chat: https://drive.redwood/demo/northbridge-retention-bench.xlsx (note: placeholder)
08:10 - Ravi: question from compliance—does the redaction model ever keep a pointer to original content in logs for debugging? we don't want any persistent pointer that could be rehydrated.
08:18 - Maya: no pointers. when redact-only writes, the stored object is the redacted payload. debug artifacts that contain original content are ephemeral and only accessible with elevated audit steps and are purged per your retention policy. in Private you can eliminate even ephemeral debug artifacts.
08:35 - Janelle: what's the escape hatch if we need to rotate redaction rules and realize we broke some business logic?
08:41 - Maya: we have rule rollbacks and a preview mode; we suggest running preview in parallel for 24-72 hours against a sample to catch regressions. also we store metrics about redaction rate and downstream errors to surface regressions quickly.
08:58 - Dan: operational question—how do we enforce retention at CDN or edge? some requests hit edge functions before your runtime.
09:05 - Ethan: good point. we recommend tagging requests at the edge with the x-redwood-retention header and enforcing it in gateway. if you can't, we provide SDKs/middleware for common edge platforms. for traffic that never reaches our runtime, you'd need your own retention controls in the edge layer.
09:23 - Lisa: i'm jotting down next steps. one more: can we run a security review with your security engineer? specific ask: KMS integration details, HSM, and data residency maps.
09:33 - Ethan: yes i'll loop in our security lead. whitepaper link: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/whitepaper (share).
09:40 - Ravi: any known incidents related to redaction failures?
09:44 - Maya: none in our customer base tied to redact-only misconfigurations, when incidents occur they're usually due to poorly tuned regexes outside the platform. we surface those via detection metrics.
09:55 - Lisa: ok let's talk pricing—how do we price request storage and redaction processing?
09:59 - Ethan: hosted pricing has two components: inference (per-token) and storage/redaction processing (per-GB and per-rule-eval). Dedicated bundles compute and storage into reserved capacity; redaction compute is included in node consumption. I'll send an example cost model for your volume.
10:16 - Janelle: does Optimize ever trade off redaction for cost? like recommend a cheaper model that could be less accurate at PII detection?
10:23 - Maya: Optimize surfaces trade-offs but it won't recommend reducing privacy checks. it may recommend moving non-sensitive bulk jobs to cheaper models or quantized variants—Optimize respects rule constraints.
10:34 - Dan: last tech question—how do you handle model outputs that leak PII from training artifacts?
10:39 - Maya: we vet model catalog and have evaluation harnesses to detect memorized PII; for private models you can fine-tune or filter with an output-safety layer.
10:49 - Ethan: we're nearing time so quick recap: we'll send SOC2 excerpts and the whitepaper; Maya will provision a pilot config in the sandbox with your regex set; Janelle will provide the sample workload; Dan will confirm VPC constraints; we'll schedule a security review with our security lead and a benchmarking session.
11:08 - Lisa: thank you. schedule the pilot and security review—we want to run the pilot in Dedicated sandbox if possible.
11:15 - Ethan: noted. we'll propose dates in the next email. thanks everyone.

References & artifacts mentioned:
- retention/console demo deck (link in chat)

Meeting end.
